release_notes.headline_internal: Every destructive MCP tool now requires the explicit LGREP_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE_MCP grant
release_notes.headline_external: Destructive maintenance calls through lgrep MCP now require an explicit server-side opt-in
highlights: All four destructive MCP tools now require LGREP_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE_MCP=1 before deleting: prune_orphans, prune_symbols, invalidate_cache, and invalidate_worktree_cache.
Without the grant, prune tools return a preview; invalidation tools safely do nothing and return a refused_reason.
The unsafe transport-based authority inference remains removed. Diagnostics still report startup transport, but it no longer uses LGREP_TRANSPORT as a runtime environment side channel.
Worktree cache invalidation documentation now accurately states that it can delete a canonical cache directory when the project is gone and no aliases remain.

breaking.description: MCP callers that previously used invalidate_cache or invalidate_worktree_cache to delete data without LGREP_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE_MCP now receive a no-op refusal.
breaking.migration: Set LGREP_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE_MCP=1 in the server environment only when destructive MCP maintenance is intended. Invalidation tools have no CLI equivalent; prune CLI --execute commands remain unchanged.
